input.public_request: Draft an implementation-ready requirements handoff for this feature request: "Add an optional punctuation style to greeting output." The handoff must be self-contained and specific enough that another engineer could implement it and write pass/fail acceptance checks without follow-up questions.

open_material_decisions: How invalid or unsupported punctuation style values must be handled.

Which punctuation styles must be supported, and what exact greeting output should each style produce.

question.prompt: This answer changes the public behavior and test cases. Which punctuation styles must the feature support in greeting output?

options.label: Two styles
options.description: Support exactly two styles: `default` and one alternate style, which keeps scope small but requires you to name the alternate and its exact output.

options.label: Several named styles
options.description: Support a fixed set of multiple named styles, which is more flexible but expands API and acceptance coverage.

options.label: Caller-defined punctuation
options.description: Let callers supply punctuation directly, which is most flexible but changes the feature from a style option into custom output control.

transcript.answer: Several named styles: support exactly `default`, `period`, `exclamation`, and `ellipsis`. Their outputs must be `Hello, {name}!`, `Hello, {name}.`, `Hello, {name}!`, and `Hello, {name}...` respectively.

open_material_decisions: How invalid or unsupported punctuation style values must be handled.

question.prompt: This answer changes the public interface and the default behavior when callers do not specify a style. How must callers choose the optional punctuation style?

options.label: Optional parameter
options.description: Add an optional `punctuationStyle` argument/property and default to `default` when omitted; this is the most conventional and easiest to test.

options.label: Separate entry points
options.description: Expose distinct APIs per style, which makes call sites explicit but expands surface area and duplicates acceptance coverage.

options.label: Config only
options.description: Select style through configuration rather than per call, which narrows runtime flexibility but may fit a centralized settings model.

transcript.answer: Callers choose the style by optionally providing a `punctuation_style` field on the request. If the field is absent, the system uses the default behavior and returns `Hello, {name}!`. If the field is present, it must be one of `default`, `period`, `exclamation`, or `ellipsis`, and its value determines only the terminal punctuation of the greeting.

contract.summary: Feature request: add an optional `punctuation_style` to greeting output. Confirmed so far: callers may provide an optional `punctuation_style` field on the request; when omitted, output must remain `Hello, {name}!`; when provided, supported values are exactly `default`, `period`, `exclamation`, and `ellipsis`; those produce `Hello, {name}!`, `Hello, {name}.`, `Hello, {name}!`, and `Hello, {name}...` respectively; the style affects only terminal punctuation. Blocking gap: behavior for invalid or unsupported `punctuation_style` values is unspecified, which materially affects observable behavior and pass/fail acceptance checks.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The optional punctuation style is under-specified, so different readers form different assumptions about what counts as punctuation style, when it applies, and which greeting outputs it should affect.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: Two reasonable implementers describe different expected outputs for the same input or ask clarifying questions about scope, defaults, or allowed styles.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: If the ambiguity is not surfaced early, the handoff cannot be implemented consistently and downstream work will diverge.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Give two people the same seed and ask each to write three example greeting outputs for default and optional cases; compare for mismatches.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The optional nature of the punctuation style is not expressed in a way that makes the user's selection or non-selection externally clear at the interface boundary.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: Observers cannot tell from the request or input whether punctuation styling was intentionally chosen, omitted, or unavailable.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: An implementable handoff needs a clear trigger condition for when the optional behavior should activate; otherwise implementation behavior becomes guesswork.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Present sample requests that include and omit the option, then ask whether the intended output variant is unambiguous in each case.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The synthesized requirements mix abstract rules and sample outputs that do not fully agree, such as examples implying punctuation changes beyond what the written rule allows.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: A reviewer can point to at least one example that cannot be derived directly from the stated requirements.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: Conflicting synthesized artifacts make the handoff non-implementable because examples and rules compete as sources of truth.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Check whether every included sample greeting can be explained step-by-step using only the written requirements.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The handoff omits key externally visible decisions such as the default output, supported option values, invalid-input behavior, or whether existing greetings remain unchanged when no option is provided.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: A receiver must invent behavior for at least one common case before writing acceptance criteria or code.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: Missing decision points force downstream invention, which breaks the goal of producing an implementable requirements handoff.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Attempt to draft acceptance checks for default case, opted-in case, and invalid option case using only the handoff; note any invented assumptions.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The expected behavior is framed too loosely to support pass-fail evaluation of outputs, especially around formatting differences that are small but user-visible.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: Multiple reviewers disagree on whether a produced greeting is correct because the acceptance target is qualitative rather than exact.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: Without precise observable outcomes, the handoff cannot reliably confirm whether the requirement was implemented as intended.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Ask reviewers to judge a small set of candidate outputs against the handoff and measure whether they reach the same verdicts.

findings.description: The handoff leaves invalid or unsupported `punctuation_style` behavior unspecified, so a receiver would still need to invent externally visible behavior before implementing or testing the feature.
findings.why_material: The public request requires an "implementation-ready requirements handoff" that another engineer can implement "without follow-up questions," but the contract itself says one material decision remains open and marks the handoff as not implementation-ready.
